entries.value: Say Allahu Akbar and prostrate again exactly as before, saying the tasbih three times. With this, one rak'ah is complete.
Stay seated for a moment after the salam. Ask Allah for forgiveness three times and say the words below, then glorify Him with the tasbih. The complete set of remembrances is in the Athkar section.
I seek Allah's forgiveness (three times). O Allah, You are Peace and from You comes peace. Blessed are You, O Possessor of majesty and honour.
Subhan Allah, Alhamdu lillah, Allahu Akbar. Then once: La ilaha illa Allah, wahdahu la sharika lah, lahul-mulku wa lahul-hamd, wa huwa ala kulli shay'in qadir.
Still seated after the blessings on the Prophet ﷺ, seek refuge with Allah from four things, then ask for whatever good you wish. This is the last supplication inside the prayer.
O Allah, I seek refuge in You from the punishment of the grave, from the punishment of Hell, from the trials of life and death, and from the evil of the trial of the False Messiah.
Final tashahhud, blessings on the Prophet ﷺ and a supplication
First tashahhud, then stand for the next rak'ah
Tap a prayer to see how its rak'ahs fit together
Opening takbir, then the opening supplication
Bow, then rise and stand upright
The salam to the right and to the left
Tap any row to open that step
Two prostrations with a short sitting between them
Wudu and prayer, step by step with pictures

• At least two rak'ahs, prayed two at a time.
• It counts as charity on behalf of every joint of the body.
• Also called the prayer of the oft-returning (al-awwabin).
From about 15 minutes after sunrise until shortly before Dhuhr; best when the sun is hot

• No adhan and no iqamah.
• First rak'ah: the opening takbir then six more takbirs before reciting.
• Second rak'ah: five takbirs after rising, before reciting.
• Recommended: Al-A'la and Al-Ghashiyah, or Qaf and Al-Qamar.
• The sermon comes after the prayer.
• Say the takbir on the way to the prayer ground.
Allah is the Greatest, Allah is the Greatest, there is no god but Allah; Allah is the Greatest, Allah is the Greatest, and to Allah belongs all praise.
Eid morning, from shortly after sunrise until noon, at the prayer ground or mosque

• Performed exactly as in the step-by-step guide.
• Recitation is aloud in Fajr and in the first two rak'ahs of Maghrib and Isha, and silent in Dhuhr and Asr.
• Al-Fatiha plus a surah in the first two rak'ahs; Al-Fatiha alone in the rest.
• A first tashahhud after the second rak'ah and a final one at the end.
Fajr: from dawn until sunrise · Dhuhr: after the sun passes its zenith · Asr: when an object's shadow equals its length · Maghrib: from sunset · Isha: after the red twilight fades, until midnight

• Pray two non-obligatory rak'ahs.
• After the salam, say the istikhara supplication, naming your matter where it says 'this matter'.
• Then proceed with whatever is made easy for you; it may be repeated.

O Allah, I seek Your guidance by Your knowledge, and Your help by Your power, and I ask You of Your great bounty. You are able and I am not, You know and I do not, and You are the Knower of the unseen. O Allah, if You know this matter is good for me in my religion, my livelihood and my final outcome, then decree it for me, make it easy for me and bless me in it. And if You know this matter is bad for me in my religion, my livelihood and my final outcome, then turn it away from me and turn me away from it, and decree for me the good wherever it may be, then make me content with it.
When undecided about a permissible matter, at any time outside the forbidden times

• People go out to the prayer ground in humility.
• Two rak'ahs like the Eid prayer with its takbirs.
• The imam gives a sermon full of seeking forgiveness and supplication, turns his cloak inside out, and people raise their hands in supplication.
• Fasting and charity beforehand are recommended.
O Allah, send us rain. O Allah, send us rain. O Allah, send us rain.
In drought when rain is withheld, usually at the time of the Eid prayer

• The imam stands by the head of a man or the middle of a woman, with rows behind him.
• First takbir: recite Al-Fatiha.
• Second: send blessings on the Prophet ﷺ (the Ibrahimi salawat).
• Third: supplicate for the deceased.
• Fourth: a brief supplication, then one salam to the right.
• Raise the hands with each takbir.

O Allah, forgive him and have mercy on him, grant him wellbeing and pardon him, honour his arrival, widen his entrance, wash him with water, snow and hail, and cleanse him of sins as a white garment is cleansed of dirt.
One standing, no bowing or prostration
After the deceased is washed and shrouded, before burial

• Obligatory on adult resident men; women, travellers and the sick pray Dhuhr instead.
• Ghusl, perfume, good clothes and arriving early are sunnah.
• The imam gives two sermons, listened to in silence.
• Two rak'ahs recited aloud after the sermons, replacing Dhuhr.
• Whoever misses it prays Dhuhr with four rak'ahs.
Friday at Dhuhr time, in congregation at the mosque

• Prayed in congregation without adhan; the call is 'As-salatu jami'ah'.
• In each rak'ah: a long standing and recitation, a long bowing, then a shorter standing and recitation, a shorter bowing, then two long prostrations.
• Recitation is aloud.
• The imam then gives a sermon urging remembrance, supplication, charity and seeking forgiveness.
From the start of a solar or lunar eclipse until it clears

• Two before Fajr.
• Four before Dhuhr (two by two) and two after it.
• Two after Maghrib.
• Two after Isha.
• Prayed two rak'ahs at a time, best at home.
• Whoever keeps them up has a house built for them in Paradise.
Just before or after the obligatory prayer, within its time

• An addition (an extra rak'ah or bowing): two prostrations after the salam.
• Omitting a required act (like the first tashahhud): two prostrations before the salam.
• Doubt about the count: build on certainty (the lower number) and prostrate before the salam; if one is more likely, go with it and prostrate after the salam.
• Two prostrations with a sitting between them, then the salam.
• Leaving out a pillar like bowing is not fixed by prostration; it must be performed.
When you forgetfully add, omit or doubt something in the prayer

• Pray standing if you can, even leaning on a stick or wall.
• Otherwise sitting, then on your side facing the Qibla, then lying on your back with your feet towards the Qibla.
• Nod the head for bowing and prostration, making prostration lower.
• If wudu is impossible, make tayammum; two prayers may be combined in hardship.
• The prayer is never dropped while the mind is present.
When illness prevents standing, bowing or prostrating

• Prayed in pairs, with a salam after every two rak'ahs.
• The Prophet ﷺ prayed eleven rak'ahs including witr.
• Lengthen the standing, bowing, prostration and supplication.
• Ask for whatever you wish in prostration.
• End it with witr.
Two at a time, no fixed number
After Isha until dawn; the last third of the night is best

• Two light rak'ahs before sitting.
• Any prayer you perform on entering (a sunnah or the obligatory prayer) counts for it.
• Not for the Friday preacher; for a visitor to the Sacred Mosque, tawaf is its greeting.
On entering the mosque, before sitting down

• Prayed two rak'ahs at a time, each pair ending with a salam.
• In congregation at the mosque is sunnah, though it is valid at home.
• Completing the Quran over the month is recommended.
• Ends with witr.

• Make wudu well, then pray two rak'ahs.
• Afterwards seek forgiveness with sincere repentance: regret, stopping the sin, resolving not to return, and restoring others' rights.
• Whoever does this is forgiven, by Allah's leave.
I seek the forgiveness of Allah, besides whom there is no god, the Ever-Living, the Sustainer, and I repent to Him.
After falling into a sin, at any time

• Shortening: Dhuhr, Asr and Isha are prayed as two rak'ahs; Fajr and Maghrib are not shortened.
• Combining: Dhuhr with Asr, and Maghrib with Isha, may be combined earlier or later when needed.
• A traveller praying behind a resident imam prays in full.
• The regular sunnahs are dropped except the Fajr sunnah and witr.
On a journey of about 80 km or more, from leaving town until returning

• At its least, one rak'ah.
• Three rak'ahs: two with a salam then one, or three together with a single tashahhud at the end.
• Recommended: Al-A'la in the first, Al-Kafirun in the second and Al-Ikhlas in the third.
• The Qunut supplication is recommended in the last rak'ah after rising from bowing (or before it).
• It is the last prayer of the night.

O Allah, guide me among those You have guided, grant me wellbeing among those You have granted wellbeing, take care of me among those You have taken care of, bless me in what You have given, and protect me from the evil of what You have decreed. You decree and none decrees over You. Whoever You befriend is never humiliated, and whoever You oppose is never honoured. Blessed are You, our Lord, and Exalted.
1, 3, 5 or more, always an odd number
After Isha until dawn; the end of the night is best if you trust yourself to wake

• Two rak'ahs after wudu, with full attention of heart and face.
• Paradise is promised to the one who prays them without letting the mind wander.
• May be prayed at any time, even in the forbidden times according to many scholars.
Beyond the basic rak'ah: what each kind of prayer is, when it is prayed, how many rak'ahs it has, and how it differs.
Intend in your heart to make wudu for prayer, then say Bismillah before you begin.
Wash both hands up to the wrists three times, starting with the right, and rub between the fingers.
Take water into your mouth with the right hand, swirl it around and spit it out, three times.
Sniff water into the nose with the right hand and blow it out with the left, three times.
Wash the whole face from the hairline to the chin and from ear to ear, three times.
Wash the right arm from the fingertips up to and including the elbow three times, then the left arm the same way.
Wet your hands and wipe over the whole head from the front to the back and back again, then wipe the inside and outside of the ears. This is done once.
Wash the right foot up to and including the ankle three times, rubbing between the toes, then the left foot the same way.
When you finish, say the testimony of faith. Your wudu is complete and you are ready to pray.
I bear witness that there is no god but Allah alone, without partner, and I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger.
Using the toilet, passing wind, deep sleep, and losing consciousness. After any of these, make wudu again before praying.

Noon or meem with shaddah: a nasal sound held for 2 counts.
Said only when you start from this word; dropped when it is joined to what comes before.
Noon sakinah or tanween before ي ن م و: merged into it, with ghunnah.
Two letters from the same point of articulation, the first silent: it merges into the second.
Two letters close in articulation, the first silent: it merges into the second.
Noon sakinah or tanween before ل or ر: merged into it, without ghunnah.
Meem sakinah before another meem: merged into it, with ghunnah.
Noon sakinah or tanween before one of the 15 ikhfa letters: hidden, with ghunnah.
Meem sakinah before ب: hidden, with ghunnah.
Noon sakinah or tanween before ب: turned into a hidden meem, with ghunnah.
Noon sakinah or tanween before a throat letter (ء ه ع ح غ خ): said clearly, without ghunnah.
Meem sakinah before any letter but م and ب: said clearly.
The lam of «ال» is silent; the sun letter after it is doubled.
A madd or leen letter before a letter made silent by stopping: 2, 4 or 6 counts when you stop.
A madd letter with no hamza or sukoon after it: 2 counts.
A madd letter followed by a permanent sukoon or shaddah: held for 6 counts.
A madd letter ending a word, with hamza starting the next: 4 or 5 counts.
A madd letter followed by hamza in the same word: 4 or 5 counts.
ق ط ب ج د with sukoon: the letter is released with a slight bounce.
